newsitem.title: USA: Dow storms higher after Friday's near-record drop.
newsitem.headline: Dow storms higher after Friday's near-record drop.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average rebounded strongly Monday as bargain hunters resurfaced after the high drama of Friday's near-record market plunge.

Based on early and unofficial data, the Dow stormed 108.70 points higher, or 1.4 percent, to 7,803.36, regaining a large chunk of the 247-point loss Friday, which was the second biggest point drop since the 1987 crash.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a narrow margin on active volume of 517 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

Analysts said the market raced higher as investors sought an entry point after Friday's plunge on concern that future corporate earnings growth may slow. But many investors were still unsure of the market's short-term direction, which accounted for the extreme volatility.
Wall Street was also trying to anticipate the outcome of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting on interest rates.
"This was a very good first step" after Friday's losses, said Brad Weekes, managing director of equity trading at Donaldson, Lufkin Jenrette & Co.
Despite the big drop in the Dow, some money managers saw little sign of assets being reallocated in investment portfolios.

"We have not seen any and we don't intend to make any," said James Walline, vice president, equities and mutual funds at Lutheran Brotherhood. "The market has stabilized this morning and frankly we don't see any reason to reallocate."
Among the big movers, Hewlett-Packard Co. fell 2-1/2 to 63-13/16 after reporting lower-than-expected quarterly results.
